zh.title: CEH M01｜C30–C38：SOC、營運持續與安全治理文件

sections.heading: 核心結論：企業資安不只要防止攻擊，更要有能力發現事件、指揮應變、維持營運，並透過文件建立明確的責任

body.text: CEH v13 · M01-07 · 9 個核心觀念 · NIST × ISO × MITRE ATT&CK × 臺美產業規範
假設一家臺灣半導體製造商，在凌晨兩點發現製造系統出現異常。
同一時間，美國矽谷的雲端供應商發出安全告警，而與該公司合作的臺灣銀行，也發現異常的系統登入紀錄。
這時，企業必須回答四個問題：

items: Detection： 誰負責發現並初步判斷異常？
Response： 誰負責深入調查、決策與指揮事件應變？
Continuity： 如果系統無法正常使用，如何維持最重要的業務？
Governance： 企業與供應商各自承諾了什麼？哪些行為被允許？哪些資訊必須保密？

body.text: 這四個問題涵蓋本單元的 C30–C38。

sections.heading: 一、九個觀念的完整知識地圖

body.text: 本次供稿將 C30–C38 歸在 M01-07，涉及 SOC 職責、營運持續與治理文件，並引用兩道原題編號 P3-Q086 和 P3-Q088。以下保留供稿的學習順序，不提供原題答案；未附的原題全文不視為已獨立查核。

rows: 資安監控中心如何運作？
誰負責第一線監控與告警分流？
誰負責深入分析與主動威脅獵捕？
誰管理 SOC 的人員、流程與績效？
發生重大事件時，誰負責協調與指揮？
發生重大中斷時，企業如何持續營運？
服務提供者承諾哪些可衡量的服務水準？
哪些資訊必須保密，誰負有保密義務？
使用者可以如何使用組織的資訊資產？

body.text: 這九個觀念不是九件互不相關的事情，而是一個連續的管理系統。

body.text: NIST 於 2025 年 4 月 3 日發布 SP 800-61 Revision 3，取代 Revision 2。新版把事件應變整合到 NIST Cybersecurity Framework（CSF）2.0 的 Govern、Identify、Protect、Detect、Respond、Recover 六大功能，將應變能力納入持續的風險管理。
接下來逐一深入。

sections.heading: 二、C30｜Security Operations Center：SOC 是什麼？

body.text: 1. 白話理解：SOC 就是資安系統的監控與應變協調中樞
想像一家大型半導體工廠。
生產設備有溫度、壓力、電流與設備狀態監控。
當某個數值異常，系統會通知工程師確認是否存在故障。
SOC 也是類似概念，只是監控對象變成資訊安全。
它可能接收：

items: 伺服器與作業系統日誌。
防火牆與網路流量紀錄。
EDR（Endpoint Detection and Response）端點告警。
雲端與身分管理系統日誌。
應用程式安全事件。
Threat Intelligence（威脅情報）。

body.text: SOC 將這些訊號轉化成有意義的安全判斷。
2. SOC 不等於一套 SIEM 軟體
這是第一個容易混淆的觀念。

rows: 負責監控、分析、分流、協調與改善安全事件處理的組織能力
集中收集、搜尋、關聯分析日誌及安全事件
偵測、調查並回應端點的可疑活動
整合安全工具與工作流程，自動化部分應變動作
提供攻擊者、技術、指標與威脅背景資訊

body.text: 所以，企業購買一套 SIEM，並不代表已經建立有效的 SOC。
真正的 SOC 還需要明確的職責、值班制度、事件標準、升級規則、處置授權及績效評估。
3. 一個 SOC 告警如何變成安全事件？
假設銀行系統發出一則告警：
「某管理員帳號在異常時間登入。」
這個訊號可能有多種解釋。
管理員可能正在合法執行夜間維護；也可能是帳號遭到入侵。
因此，SOC 的工作不是看到異常就直接判定企業遭受攻擊，而是建立證據。

body.text: NIST CSF 2.0 對此有非常直接的對應：

items: DE.AE-02： 分析潛在不利事件。
DE.AE-03： 關聯多個資訊來源。
DE.AE-07： 整合威脅情報與其他背景資訊。
DE.AE-08： 當符合事件判定條件時，宣告資安事件。
RS.MA-03： 對已識別事件分類並排定優先順序。
RS.MA-04： 必要時進行事件升級。

body.text: 上述內容可以直接從 NIST CSF 2.0 官方繁體中文版核對。
4. 如何利用 MITRE ATT&CK？
假設 SOC 發現：
某個原本只在正常上班時間使用的外部維修帳號，凌晨透過 VPN 登入半導體公司的維護系統。
MITRE ATT&CK T1078 — Valid Accounts 描述攻擊者濫用有效帳號的行為。查核時現行頁面列出的戰術包括 Initial Access（初始存取）、Persistence（持續存取）、Privilege Escalation（權限提升）及 Stealth（隱蔽）；有效帳號也可能讓活動混入正常使用模式。
SOC 可以利用 ATT&CK 建立調查假說：
「這是否為合法維修，或是被竊取的有效帳號遭到濫用？」
接著關聯登入紀錄、MFA、工單、設備維護時段，以及是否出現非預期的後續行為。
但必須記住：某個行為符合 ATT&CK 技術描述，不代表已經證明攻擊發生。 ATT&CK 是攻擊行為知識庫，不能單獨代替證據驗證。
C30 核心：SOC 的真正功能，是把分散的安全訊號轉化為可採取行動的事件判斷與處置流程。

sections.heading: 三、C31｜Tier 1 Analyst：第一線分析人員為什麼重要？

body.text: 1. Tier 1 就像急診的檢傷分流
醫院急診收到病人後，不是所有病人都立即進入手術室。
首先需要確認症狀、危急程度，以及應交由哪個專業團隊處理。
SOC 的 Tier 1 Analyst 也有類似職責。
Tier 1 的主要工作是初步監控、驗證、分流及升級安全告警。
它不代表只能按下「確認」按鈕，而是要在有限時間內做出有根據的第一線判斷。
2. 一則告警應如何處理？
假設臺灣銀行的 SIEM 偵測到某位管理員帳號：
凌晨 02:00 從未見過的來源登入雲端管理平台。
Tier 1 應先查核幾個重要事實：

items: 這個帳號的正常登入模式是什麼？
是否有已核准的夜間維護工單？
MFA 與身分驗證紀錄是否正常？
是否存在異常的後續存取或大量資料下載？
是否符合預先定義的事件升級條件？

body.text: 得到證據後，才能適當分類。

rows: 告警條件觸發，但證據不支持所警示的問題
記錄原因、調整偵測規則
存在異常，但尚不足以確定
已符合組織定義的資安事件條件
啟動相應事件應變程序

body.text: 初步分流不只是確認真假，也要評估潛在影響與急迫性。
例如，企業網站上的單次失敗登入，與晶圓廠製造設備的管理員帳號遭異常使用，即使告警種類相似，處理優先順序也可能截然不同。
3. Tier 1 的技術能力
Tier 1 應具備基本的網路、作業系統、身分驗證、日誌分析及安全事件概念。
同時，必須知道自己的處置權限。
例如，Tier 1 可以依據預先核准的 Playbook（應變操作手冊）執行特定操作，但不代表每位 Tier 1 都有權停止銀行正式交易系統。
對照標準： NIST CSF 2.0 的 DE.AE-06、DE.AE-08，以及 RS.MA-02–04，分別涉及事件資訊傳遞、事件判定、事件報告驗證、優先排序與升級。
C31 核心：第一線分析人員的價值，是及時把大量原始告警轉換成可靠的判斷，而不是把所有告警一律升級。

sections.heading: 四、C32｜Tier 3 Analyst / Threat Hunter：為什麼不能只等系統告警？

body.text: 1. 偵測不到，不代表沒有攻擊
假設半導體公司的防毒、EDR 和防火牆都沒有產生告警。
這是否意味著企業沒有遭到入侵？
不能這樣推論。
原因包括：

items: 攻擊者可能利用正常帳號登入。
攻擊行為可能沒有觸發現有偵測規則。
某些資料來源可能沒有被收集。
安全工具可能被規避或失效。
攻擊者可能已長期存在於環境中。

body.text: 因此，需要主動威脅獵捕（Threat Hunting）。
2. Tier 3 與 Threat Hunting 是同一件事嗎？
不完全是。
許多 SOC 會將 Tier 3 設計成進階分析人員，負責複雜事件調查、進階威脅分析及改善偵測能力。
Threat Hunter 則是專門主動尋找尚未被既有告警系統發現的威脅。
在部分企業，Threat Hunter 是 Tier 3 的工作之一；在其他企業，威脅獵捕可能由獨立團隊執行。
Tier 1、Tier 2、Tier 3 是常見的 SOC 組織分層，並不是 NIST 強制規定的全產業職稱。

NIST SP 800-181 Rev. 1（2020）提供 NICE Framework 的結構，重視實際工作任務、知識與技能。Work Roles 等元件另行維護；查核時的 Components v2.2.0（2026 年 4 月 28 日）區分 Defensive Cybersecurity、Incident Response、Threat Analysis 等角色。這些角色名稱應歸屬元件目錄，不能全部當成 2020 年文件中的原始職稱。
3. 威脅獵捕與一般告警處理的差異

rows: 研究人員提出威脅假說
主動搜尋潛在攻擊證據
威脅發現、偵測改善、涵蓋缺口

body.text: 4. 使用 MITRE ATT&CK 建立獵捕假說
假設我們懷疑半導體公司的外部設備供應商帳號遭到濫用。
可以從 MITRE ATT&CK T1078（Valid Accounts）建立假說：
攻擊者可能利用合法帳號登入，但其登入時間、來源設備及後續操作不同於正常維護模式。
接著驗證：

items: 維護帳號是否在未核准時段登入？
是否來自非預期的 VPN 或網路來源？
是否存取正常職務範圍以外的系統？
是否出現非預期的權限提升？
是否可以與其他端點及系統日誌交叉驗證？

body.text: ATT&CK T1078 的現行技術頁也提供異常登入、服務帳號濫用及雲端身分行為等偵測分析範例。
但要注意一個研究方法上的問題：
假設獵捕沒有發現異常，不代表可以證明攻擊者不存在。
因為可能仍存在 Telemetry Coverage Gap（遙測涵蓋缺口）。
所以好的 Threat Hunting 報告，除了說明找到什麼，也應記錄搜尋範圍、資料來源、假設條件、觀察期間及未知區域。
C32 核心：Tier 3 處理更複雜的安全分析；Threat Hunting 的重要特色，是在尚未收到明確告警時，主動尋找隱藏的攻擊證據。

sections.heading: 五、C33｜SOC Manager：管理 SOC，不等於指揮每一場資安事故

body.text: 1. SOC Manager 是資安監控能力的管理者
假設一家矽谷科技公司有 12 名 SOC 分析師，輪班監控多個雲端產品。
SOC Manager 必須考慮的不只是技術問題，還包括人員、流程、預算與交付品質。
典型工作包括管理排班、教育訓練、事件分流流程、工具品質、服務承諾、案件積壓與持續改善。
例如：
如果同一條 SIEM 規則每天產生 2,000 則沒有調查價值的告警，分析師可能疲於處理雜訊，反而忽略真正重要的事件。
這不是單一 Tier 1 可以完全解決的問題。
SOC Manager 應要求改善偵測規則，合理配置資源，並檢查流程是否仍能達到安全目標。
2. 如何量測 SOC 的運作品質？

rows: 從定義的事件起點到偵測，平均需要多久？
告警出現後，多久有人確認接手？
Mean Time to Respond / Recover 等
依明確定義衡量回應、修復或恢復時間。
FP/(FP+TN)：實際為陰性的觀測中，被誤判為陽性的比例。FP 是誤報，TN 是正確陰性；告警中的誤報比例另為 FP/(TP+FP)，其中 TP 是正確陽性，兩個分母不可混用。
被升級的案件是否具有足夠證據與正確優先順序？

body.text: 若 SOC 要評估分析師收到的告警有多少是雜訊，可另量測告警中的誤報比例 FP/(TP+FP)，而不是套用 FPR 名稱。兩項量測都需要清楚的觀察期間、案件判定依據與分母；只對告警案件抽樣，通常無法直接取得全部 TN，也就不能單憑該抽樣估計完整 FPR。
這些是常見營運量測指標，不是所有 SOC 都必須使用相同名稱及公式。
尤其 MTTR 在不同組織可能分別指 Mean Time to Respond、Repair、Resolve 或 Recover，正式使用時必須明確定義起訖點。
3. 為什麼不能只追求快速結案？
假設主管設定：
「所有告警必須在五分鐘內結案。」
分析師為了達成 KPI，可能把缺乏證據的事件直接標成誤報。
結果報表非常漂亮，但 SOC 的偵測品質下降。
這是一個典型的代理指標問題（Proxy Metric Problem）。
真正的目標不是縮短工單存在時間，而是在合理成本下，提高偵測、分析與應變的正確性及時效性。
因此，SOC Manager 應將處理時效和案例抽樣覆核、漏報檢查、偵測涵蓋率及應變結果一起評估。
C33 核心：SOC Manager 對 SOC 的持續運作與管理品質負責，不必然是每一場重大事件的現場指揮官。

sections.heading: 六、C34｜Incident Response Commander：重大事件發生後，誰有權決定下一步？

body.text: 1. 一場重大資安事件，需要跨部門決策
假設某半導體工廠的設備維護管理系統疑似遭入侵。
資安團隊提議立即隔離相關伺服器。
但是製造部門指出：
「現在直接斷線，可能造成設備失去必要的管理功能，進而影響生產與實體安全。」
法務部門也提醒，部分日誌需要保存，以供後續調查。
這時候，如果所有部門各自採取行動，可能產生更大的問題。
Incident Response Commander（事件應變指揮者）的核心職責，就是在預先賦予的權限內，統一協調事件應變。
2. 指揮者不一定是技術最強的人
Incident Commander 不必親自分析所有封包、記憶體映像或惡意程式。
他必須能整合各專業團隊的判斷，處理優先順序、權限及衝突。

3. 事件應變的關鍵決策
Incident Commander 可能需要主持以下判斷：

rows: 是否宣告重大資安事件？
技術證據、業務影響、事件判定準則
持續攻擊風險、隔離後果、替代方案
服務受損程度、關鍵業務可持續能力
是否通知客戶或主管機關？
事件事實、契約與適用通報義務
系統可信狀態、修復驗證及業務核准

body.text: 關鍵不是所有事情都由指揮者自行決定，而是依據事先建立的權限與決策規則，讓有權責的人及時作出可追溯的決策。
NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3 將事件應變視為持續的風險管理能力。NIST CSF 2.0 的 RS.MA-01–05 則涵蓋應變計畫執行、事件驗證、排序、升級及啟動復原準則。
4. SOC Manager 與 Incident Commander 的本質差異

rows: 情勢判斷、應變決策、協調
事件控制、復原與結案結果

body.text: 在規模較小的企業，同一個人可能兼任兩者；但角色的權責仍應分開定義。
C34 核心：事件指揮者負責把跨部門的資訊轉變成一致、及時、可追溯的應變行動。

sections.heading: 七、C35｜Business Continuity Plan（BCP）：災難發生時，企業如何繼續營運？

body.text: 1. BCP 不是「如何把伺服器重新開機」
假設一家銀行的網路銀行系統遭受勒索軟體攻擊。
IT 團隊可能需要數小時才能恢復相關伺服器。
但是銀行不能只回答：
「我們正在修電腦。」
銀行還要思考：

items: 哪些重要金融業務必須持續？
是否有替代交易或服務管道？
哪些業務可以暫時延後？
客戶如何得知服務狀態？
其他銀行系統是否受到影響？
什麼時候能恢復到可接受的服務能力？

body.text: 這就是 BCP 的目的。
Business Continuity Plan（營運持續計畫）描述組織在重大中斷發生期間及之後，如何持續維持必要的業務功能。
NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 將 BCP 定義為一組預先建立的程序，用來確保重要業務流程在重大中斷期間及之後持續運作。
BCP 所處理的範圍不只包含資安事故，也可能包括地震、停電、供應鏈中斷、設備故障或其他重大事件。
2. BCP、DRP 與 Incident Response Plan 的差異
這三份文件極容易混淆。

rows: 發生資安事件時，如何調查、控制及處置？
發生重大災難後，如何恢復受影響系統與基礎設施？
正常系統無法使用期間，如何維持關鍵業務？

body.text: 假設一家半導體公司的 MES（Manufacturing Execution System，製造執行系統）發生重大異常。
IRP 關心是否遭到惡意入侵，以及如何隔離、調查與控制事件。
DRP 關心如何使用備援資源與可信備份，恢復 MES 的技術功能。
BCP 則進一步關心 MES 無法正常運作時，哪些製造活動必須暫停、哪些可依核准的替代程序執行，以及如何確保人員與設備安全。
這三種計畫可以彼此配合，但不能互相替代。
3. Business Impact Analysis（BIA）：企業為什麼需要先決定什麼最重要？
BCP 的基礎之一是 BIA（業務衝擊分析）。
BIA 不只是列出所有系統，而是要回答：
如果某項業務中斷 10 分鐘、1 小時、1 天，分別會造成什麼後果？
例如：

rows: 製程排程或生產控制受影響
客戶交易無法正常處理
核心系統、支付通道、網路
客戶無法使用平台功能

body.text: ISO 22301:2019 是營運持續管理系統（BCMS）的國際要求標準，ISO/TS 22317:2021 則專門提供 BIA 的實施指引。
4. RTO 與 RPO：兩個數字不能搞混
RTO（Recovery Time Objective）：復原時間目標。
描述系統或服務應在多長的目標時間內恢復到所要求的狀態。
RPO（Recovery Point Objective）：復原點目標。
描述系統復原後，資料至少需要恢復到事故前的哪個時間點；在常見時間差表示法中，可以理解為容忍多少時間範圍內的資料損失。

body.name: recoverytimeline
body.caption: 銀行交易系統示例：RPO 15 分鐘、RTO 2 小時
body.description: 以下數字僅供教學，是目標而非實測結果或固定法規要求。RPO 關心資料損失的時間範圍；RTO 關心恢復服務所需的時間。兩者必須分別經過備份、復原與演練驗證。線段依 15：120（1：8）呈現真正時間比例，文字獨立排列以免窄螢幕標籤重疊。 本教學例以事故點 0 作為 RTO 計時基準；實務起訖點依業務需求與復原計畫明確定義，不表示所有 NIST 情境一律從事故點起算。

items.title: 復原點｜事故前 15 分鐘（−15 min）
items.body: RPO（Recovery Point Objective）= 15 分鐘：資料復原點目標。

items.title: 事故｜0 min
items.body: 時間軸基準點：系統中斷開始。

items.title: 復原目標｜事故後 2 小時（+120 min）
items.body: RTO（Recovery Time Objective）= 2 小時：恢復所需服務能力的目標。事故到此目標之間為系統中斷及復原期間。

body.text: NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 的術語定義也明確區分 Recovery Time Objective 與 Recovery Point Objective。
這裡還有一個重要的邏輯：
即使企業每 15 分鐘備份一次，也不代表一定能達成 RPO 15 分鐘，更不代表能在兩小時內完成復原。
還需要考慮備份是否成功、是否有一致性、備份有沒有受到破壞，以及實際復原速度。
5. 臺灣金融監理對營運持續的要求
金管會《金融控股公司及銀行業內部控制及稽核制度實施辦法》第 12 條，明確將營運持續管理機制列為內部控制應涵蓋的政策與作業程序。
同條也要求涵蓋重大偶發事件處理及客戶資料保密。
金融機構需要把這些要求落實到實際業務與系統，而不是只有一份文件。
銀行公會的《金融機構資通安全防護基準》及《金融機構辦理電子銀行業務安全控管作業基準》則是查核相關安全實務時應參考的自律規範。
6. ISO 22301 的定位
ISO 22301 是 BCMS 的要求標準，而 BCP 是營運持續管理體系中的一項重要計畫與交付物。
截至 2026 年 11 月，ISO 22301:2019 仍是正式發布的主要版本，另有 Amd 1:2024 修訂；後續修訂尚處於開發階段。
C35 核心：BCP 要維持的是重要業務，不只是讓 IT 系統重新上線。

sections.heading: 八、C36｜Service Level Agreement（SLA）：服務承諾如何轉換成可驗證的責任？

body.text: 1. SLA 就是對服務品質與責任的具體約定
假設一家矽谷雲端公司向臺灣銀行提供 AI API。
供應商說：
「我們的系統非常穩定，而且有專業客服。」
這句話沒有具體衡量標準。
銀行無法清楚知道何時算服務失敗、供應商多久必須回應，或服務不符合承諾時應如何處理。
因此需要 SLA。
NIST 對 Service Level Agreement 的定義，涵蓋服務提供者的責任、客戶期待、可靠性、服務水準、回應時間，以及通報、解決與終止等約定。
2. 一份完整的 SLA 可以約定什麼？

rows: 嚴重事件通報後的首次回應時間
修復或恢復的目標與責任
使用什麼監控資料計算服務水準
提供服務報告的頻率及方式
哪些情況不計入特定指標
未達服務承諾時的補救方式

body.text: 以上是設計 SLA 時可以採用的項目，具體條件必須由當事方約定。
3. 99.9% 的可用率代表什麼？
假設某份 SLA 承諾，按照其定義，每月服務可用率達到 99.9%。
若以 30 天、24 小時的完整月份計算，而且沒有額外排除項目：
也就是整個月份容許約 43.2 分鐘的不符合可用性條件時間。
但是，真正的 SLA 必須先定義什麼算「不可用」，以及如何計算。
例如，登入頁面正常，但主要交易 API 全部失敗，究竟算不算服務可用？
如果 SLA 只用不適當的健康檢查端點衡量，可能出現監控顯示服務正常、客戶實際無法使用的情況。
所以 SLA 不只是數字，而是可以驗證的服務定義。
4. SLA、RTO、RPO 的重要差別

rows: 供應商提供什麼服務品質？
服務合約與供應商治理
是否一定具有相同約束力？
視企業目標及契約／法規要求
視企業目標及契約／法規要求

body.text: 一家供應商可以同時承諾可用率及 RTO，但兩者不能互相推論。
而且 SLA 不一定涵蓋所有系統故障情境，必須查看實際約定。
C36 核心：SLA 是服務水準與責任的約定，不是營運持續計畫，也不是保密契約。

sections.heading: 九、C37｜Non-Disclosure Agreement（NDA）：保密協議在保護什麼？

body.text: 1. NDA 的目的，不是讓資訊永遠不能使用
假設臺灣半導體公司委託美國資安顧問，檢查製程資料交換平台。
顧問可能需要接觸：

items: 系統架構圖。
資料庫結構。
尚未公開的技術資訊。
測試過程取得的漏洞資訊。
客戶或供應商的機密資料。

body.text: 這些資訊是為了完成特定工作而提供，不代表顧問可以任意複製、利用或公開。
所以雙方需要明確約定保密責任。
NDA（Non-Disclosure Agreement）是一種以契約方式約束特定資訊使用、保存與揭露的協議。
它可以是雙方相互承擔保密義務的 Mutual NDA，也可以是單方承擔保密義務的 Unilateral NDA。
2. 完整的 NDA 應回答哪些問題？

rows: 資訊可以用於什麼目的？
接收方應採取哪些保密措施？
哪些資訊不受保密條款限制？
合作結束後如何返還或清理資訊？
遇到適用法律要求揭露時如何處理？

body.text: 特別重要的是，NDA 不應被設計成妨礙依法向主管機關通報或其他受法律保護的揭露活動。
3. 臺灣半導體：NDA 與《營業秘密法》的關係
臺灣《營業秘密法》第 2 條規定，受保護資訊需要符合秘密性、因秘密性具有經濟價值，以及所有人已採取合理保密措施等要件。
第 10 條則將特定以不正當方法取得、使用或洩漏營業秘密的行為納入侵害範圍，其中包括違反保密義務等不正當方法。
因此，NDA 可以成為企業合理保密措施的重要組成部分。
但不能反向推論：
「只要文件上寫了 Confidential，或者雙方簽署 NDA，所有資訊就必然構成法律上的營業秘密。」
仍須檢視法定要件及實際保護措施。
4. 美國矽谷：《Defend Trade Secrets Act》
美國聯邦法律 18 U.S.C. §1839(3) 也要求營業秘密所有人採取合理保密措施，且資訊因不為一般人所知而具有獨立經濟價值。
18 U.S.C. §1833(b) 對特定保密揭露提供美國聯邦及州營業秘密法下的民事與刑事責任免責：向美國聯邦、州或地方政府官員，或向律師保密揭露，且僅為通報或調查疑似違法行為。這不是所有揭露行為的概括免責；§1833(b)(5) 也不授權以其他違法方式取得營業秘密。
這說明 NDA 的保密義務需要與適用法律共同理解。
5. NDA 與 C15 弱點揭露的連結
假設資安顧問發現半導體平台有重大漏洞。
顧問應依照授權與約定的回報管道，提供經過適當保護的測試證據。
但 NDA 不會自動取代：

items: 測試授權書。
Scope 與 ROE。
弱點回報流程。
資安事件通報程序。
資料刪除及清理要求。

body.text: 這些文件規範不同的問題，需要相互協調。
C37 核心：NDA 處理的是特定資訊的保密、使用與揭露義務，不是服務可用率，也不是系統操作許可。

sections.heading: 十、C38｜Acceptable Use Policy（AUP）：企業為什麼需要可接受使用政策？

body.text: 1. 有系統使用權，不代表可以任意使用
假設某位銀行工程師擁有公司核發的筆記型電腦。
這台電腦由他日常使用，但他是否可以：

items: 將客戶資料上傳到個人雲端硬碟？
使用私人 AI 服務分析銀行內部文件？
安裝未經核准的遠端控制軟體？
將公司設備借給其他人使用？
把正式環境資料複製到自己的測試電腦？

body.text: 這些問題不是靠防火牆就能全部解決。
企業必須對資訊資產的合理用途與禁止行為建立明確規則。
這就是 AUP。
2. AUP 與 Access Control 有何不同？
Access Control 是技術上能否進行特定操作。
Acceptable Use Policy 是組織制度上是否允許該行為。
例如，某員工可能技術上能夠安裝一套軟體，但企業政策規定正式環境不得安裝未核准工具。
所以：
技術上可以執行  ⇏  組織政策允許執行
這正是 Governance（治理）與 Technical Controls（技術控制）之間的重要區別。
3. NIST SP 800-53 的正式對應
NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 的 PL-4 — Rules of Behavior，要求組織向需要存取系統的人員提供資訊及系統使用相關的責任與行為規則，取得必要的知悉與遵守確認，並定期檢討規則。
其補充指引也將 Acceptable Use Agreements 和 Non-Disclosure Agreements 列為相關的存取協議類型。
因此，AUP 不應只是入職時簽署一次、之後再也不檢討的文件。
4. 三種產業的 AUP 如何設計？

headers: 可建立的 AUP 管理規則
rows: 設備維護電腦、USB、製程資料
限制未核准軟體、外接媒體及資料外傳
SaaS 開發環境、雲端憑證、程式碼
定義個人雲端、外部 AI 工具、正式環境憑證的使用規則
客戶資料、交易系統、行員設備
限制客戶資料查詢、個人裝置使用與未核准服務

body.text: 這些是可依風險採用的企業政策設計，不代表每一家企業都有完全相同的法律條文要求。
對臺灣銀行業而言，金管會《金融控股公司及銀行業內部控制及稽核制度實施辦法》第 12 條要求內部控制涵蓋資訊管理及客戶資料保密，第 25 條則規範資訊安全制度、風險控管及事件通報應變。AUP 可以成為落實制度的一項組織控制措施。
5. AUP 如何變成可驗證的控制？
真正有效的 AUP 應與技術控制相互配合。
例如：

rows: 禁止將機密資料傳至私人雲端
禁止未授權使用 USB 儲存設備

body.text: 這些技術控制不一定能阻止所有違規行為，但可以協助企業預防、偵測並驗證政策執行情況。
C38 核心：AUP 定義資訊資產被允許如何使用；它是治理規則，不是服務水準或保密協議。

sections.heading: 十一、四份治理文件的決策矩陣

body.text: 這是整個單元最值得記住的比較表。

rows: 關鍵流程、替代措施、復原
臺灣營業秘密法、美國 DTSA

body.text: 一個實用記憶方法：
BCP 管營運不中斷；SLA 管服務承諾；NDA 管資訊保密；AUP 管資產使用。
再加上 C30–C34 的角色分工，就形成：
「由 SOC 發現問題、由事件應變組織協調處置、透過 BCP 維持營運，並以 SLA、NDA、AUP 明確化責任。」

sections.heading: 十二、三大產業的整合治理實務

body.text: 1. 臺灣半導體科技產業
假設設備供應商的遠端維修帳號遭到濫用。
SOC： 偵測異常登入與後續操作，建立事件證據。
Incident Response： 與設備工程、IT、OT 及業務管理人員協調，避免不適當的隔離措施危及製程安全。
BCP： 確保工廠可以按照已核准的替代程序，維持必要製造活動或安全停機。
SLA： 與設備或雲端供應商約定回應及服務恢復責任。
NDA／AUP： 規範供應商對製程資料的保密義務、遠端工具與帳號的允許用途。
可以參照 NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3、SEMI E187，以及臺灣《營業秘密法》第 2、10 條。
其中 NIST、SEMI 為技術及產業標準，《營業秘密法》則具有法律效力。
2. 美國矽谷科技產業
假設一家 SaaS 公司的管理員帳號遭到入侵，攻擊者可能接觸客戶資料。
SOC 負責偵測與分析；Incident Commander 協調工程、法務、客戶服務及管理階層；BCP 確保重要產品功能持續運作。
在治理上，SLA 約束服務承諾，NDA 管理供應商取得的機密資訊，AUP 則規範內部管理員及開發人員的系統使用。
技術上可以引用 NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3、NIST SP 800-53、OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet 及 MITRE ATT&CK T1078。
美國《Defend Trade Secrets Act》對營業秘密的構成要件及相關保護提供法律依據；但每項 SLA、NDA 或 AUP 的實際效力仍取決於適用法律和具體約定。
3. 金管會監理下的臺灣金融機構
假設銀行的核心金融服務遭到重大網路攻擊。

事件 B： Tier 1 無法確認帳號是否遭入侵。進階分析人員進一步發現帳號曾從未核准的設備登入。
事件 C： 資安團隊建議立即隔離設備管理伺服器，但製造部門擔心隔離造成生產中斷。
事件 D： 美國 SaaS 平台隨後停止提供服務，造成臺灣半導體公司無法取得必要維修資訊。

4. 契約治理： 事件 E 中，SLA 的月可用率與 RTO 為什麼不能直接畫上等號？若你是採購方，會要求補強哪些服務承諾？

6. 監理與供應鏈： 如果這套系統也影響臺灣銀行的重要業務，銀行應如何運用金管會的內控制度規定，以及銀行公會的資訊安全與供應鏈規範，建立事件通報、供應商監督與營運持續程序？

本單元最重要的結論：資安事件的成熟處理方式，是由可靠的偵測開始，經過明確的責任與決策流程，維持必要業務，最後透過證據、制度與契約完成改善。

sections.heading: Core conclusion: enterprise security needs the ability to prevent attacks, detect incidents, direct response, sustain operations, and establish clear responsibilities through documentation

body.text: CEH v13 · M01-07 · Nine core concepts · NIST × ISO × MITRE ATT&CK × Taiwanese and US industry requirements
Suppose that a Taiwanese semiconductor manufacturer discovers abnormal activity in its manufacturing systems at two in the morning.
At the same time, a Silicon Valley cloud provider issues a security alert, while a Taiwanese bank working with the manufacturer also discovers unusual system login records.
The enterprise must answer four questions:

items: Detection: who discovers abnormalities and makes the initial assessment?
Response: who investigates in depth, makes decisions, and directs incident response?
Continuity: how can the most important business activities continue if systems cannot operate normally?
Governance: what have the enterprise and suppliers each committed to? Which activities are permitted? Which information must remain confidential?

body.text: These four questions span this unit's C30–C38 concepts.

Not every alert requires Tier 3, major incident response or BCP activation. SLA, NDA and AUP are parallel governance documents, not sequential steps.

body.text: NIST published SP 800-61 Revision 3 on April 3, 2025, superseding Revision 2. It integrates incident response across the six NIST CSF 2.0 functions—Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond and Recover—as an ongoing risk-management capability.
We now examine each concept in detail.

sections.heading: II. C30 | Security Operations Center: what is a SOC?

body.text: 1. Plain-language explanation: the SOC is a center for security monitoring and response coordination
Imagine a large semiconductor fab.
Its production equipment is monitored for temperature, pressure, electrical current, and equipment status.
When a measurement becomes abnormal, the system notifies an engineer to check for a fault.
A SOC follows a similar idea, with information security as its subject.
It may receive:

items: Server and operating-system logs.
Firewall and network traffic records.
Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) alerts.
Cloud and identity-management logs.
Application security events.
Threat intelligence.

body.text: The SOC converts these signals into meaningful security judgments.
2. A SOC is more than SIEM software
This is an easily confused distinction.

rows: Organizational capability for monitoring, analysis, triage, coordination, and improvement of security incident handling
Centralized collection, search, and correlation of logs and security events
Detection, investigation, and response to suspicious endpoint activity
Integration of security tools and workflows, automating some response actions
Information about attackers, techniques, indicators, and threat context

body.text: Purchasing a SIEM does not establish an effective SOC by itself.
A functioning SOC also requires clear responsibilities, duty arrangements, incident criteria, escalation rules, response authority, and performance assessment.
3. How does a SOC alert become a security incident?
Suppose that a banking system issues an alert:
“An administrator account logged in at an unusual time.”
There may be several explanations.
The administrator might be performing authorized overnight maintenance, or the account might be compromised.
The SOC therefore gathers evidence instead of immediately declaring an attack whenever something is unusual.

body.name: alerttriage
body.caption: From security signals to incident determination and escalation when needed
body.description: Incident Determination uses predefined criteria to decide whether to declare an incident. An anomaly or alert alone does not establish a confirmed incident. Subsequent action follows severity and response authority.

items.title: Telemetry / Logs
items.body: Receive login time, source, account and endpoint information

items.title: Alert
items.body: Rules or analytics flag suspicious activity

items.title: Triage
items.body: Compare authorized changes, account behavior and other logs

items.title: Incident Determination
items.body: Use predefined criteria to decide whether to declare an incident

items.title: Escalation / Response
items.body: Notify appropriate personnel and act according to incident severity

body.text: NIST CSF 2.0 directly addresses these activities:

items: DE.AE-02: analyze potentially adverse events.
DE.AE-03: correlate information from multiple sources.
DE.AE-07: integrate threat intelligence and other contextual information.
DE.AE-08: declare incidents when incident criteria are met.
RS.MA-03: categorize and prioritize identified incidents.
RS.MA-04: escalate incidents when necessary.

body.text: These points can be checked in the official Traditional Chinese translation of NIST CSF 2.0.
4. How can MITRE ATT&CK help?
Suppose that the SOC discovers:
An external maintenance account normally used only during business hours logs into the semiconductor company's maintenance system through a VPN in the early morning.

MITRE ATT&CK T1078 — Valid Accounts describes adversarial abuse of valid accounts. At review, its current tactics include Initial Access, Persistence, Privilege Escalation and Stealth; valid accounts can also help activity blend into normal usage patterns.
The SOC can use ATT&CK to formulate an investigative hypothesis:
“Is this authorized maintenance, or misuse of stolen valid credentials?”
It then correlates login records, MFA, work orders, equipment maintenance windows, and any unexpected subsequent behavior.
Behavior matching an ATT&CK technique description does not prove that an attack occurred. ATT&CK is a knowledge base of adversary behavior and cannot replace evidence verification.
C30's central concept: the SOC turns dispersed security signals into actionable incident judgments and handling processes.

sections.heading: III. C31 | Tier 1 Analyst: why do frontline analysts matter?

body.text: 1. Tier 1 resembles triage in an emergency department
Patients arriving at an emergency department do not all go directly into surgery.
First, staff establish symptoms, urgency, and the appropriate specialist team.
The SOC's Tier 1 Analyst has comparable responsibilities.
Tier 1 primarily performs initial monitoring, validation, triage, and escalation of security alerts.
The role requires evidence-based frontline judgments within limited time, beyond merely clicking an acknowledgement button.
2. How should an alert be handled?
Suppose that a Taiwanese bank's SIEM detects an administrator account:
Logging into a cloud management platform at 02:00 from a previously unseen source.
Tier 1 should first check several important facts:

items: What is the account's normal login pattern?
Is there an approved overnight maintenance work order?
Are the MFA and authentication records normal?
Is there unusual subsequent access or a large data download?
Are predefined escalation criteria met?

body.text: Appropriate classification follows the evidence.

rows: An alert condition triggered, but evidence does not support the reported issue
Record the reason and tune the detection rule
An abnormality exists, but the evidence is insufficient for a conclusion
Gather evidence and escalate if necessary
The organization's defined incident criteria are met
Activate the relevant incident response process

body.text: Initial triage assesses potential impact and urgency as well as whether an alert is valid.

For example, one failed login to a corporate website and abnormal use of an administrator account on wafer-fab equipment may require very different priorities, even if the alert types resemble each other.
3. Technical capabilities for Tier 1
Tier 1 needs basic knowledge of networking, operating systems, authentication, log analysis, and security incidents.
Analysts must also understand the limits of their response authority.
For example, Tier 1 may perform particular actions under a preapproved playbook. That does not authorize every Tier 1 analyst to stop a bank's production transaction systems.
Standards mapping: NIST CSF 2.0 DE.AE-06, DE.AE-08, and RS.MA-02–04 address communication of event information, incident declaration, validation of incident reports, prioritization, and escalation.
C31's central concept: frontline analysts promptly turn numerous raw alerts into reliable judgments instead of escalating every alert indiscriminately.

sections.heading: IV. C32 | Tier 3 Analyst / Threat Hunter: why not simply wait for alerts?

body.text: 1. An absence of detection does not establish an absence of attack
Suppose that a semiconductor company's antivirus, EDR, and firewalls produce no alerts.
Does this mean that the company has not been compromised?
That inference is not justified.
Possible reasons include:

items: An attacker may log in with a normal account.
Attack activity may not trigger existing detection rules.
Some data sources may not be collected.
Security tools may be evaded or fail.
An attacker may have remained in the environment for a long time.

body.text: This creates a need for proactive threat hunting.
2. Are Tier 3 and threat hunting the same thing?
Not entirely.
Many SOCs use Tier 3 for advanced analysts responsible for complex investigations, advanced threat analysis, and improving detection capabilities.
A Threat Hunter proactively searches for threats that existing alerting systems have not identified.
In some organizations, threat hunting is part of Tier 3; elsewhere, an independent team performs it.
Tier 1, Tier 2, and Tier 3 are common SOC organizational layers, rather than industry-wide job titles mandated by NIST.

NIST SP 800-181 Rev. 1 (2020) defines the NICE Framework's structure around tasks, knowledge and skills. Work Roles and other components are maintained separately. At review, Components v2.2.0 (April 28, 2026) distinguishes roles such as Defensive Cybersecurity, Incident Response and Threat Analysis. These names belong to the component catalog and should not all be attributed as original job titles in the 2020 publication.
3. Threat hunting compared with routine alert handling

rows: A security tool generates an alert
An analyst develops a threat hypothesis
Proactively search for potential attack evidence
Threat discoveries, detection improvements, and coverage gaps

body.text: 4. Building a hunting hypothesis with MITRE ATT&CK
Suppose that we suspect misuse of an external equipment supplier's account at a semiconductor company.
Use MITRE ATT&CK T1078, Valid Accounts, to formulate a hypothesis:
An attacker may log in with a legitimate account while using times, source devices, and subsequent actions that differ from normal maintenance patterns.
Then check:

items: Does the maintenance account log in outside approved windows?
Does it originate from an unexpected VPN or network source?
Does it access systems outside its normal duties?
Is there unexpected privilege escalation?
Can endpoint and system logs corroborate the activity?

body.text: The current ATT&CK T1078 page also provides detection analysis examples for anomalous logins, service-account misuse, and cloud identity behavior.
Consider a limitation of the investigation method:
A hunt that finds no abnormalities does not prove that no attacker is present.
Telemetry Coverage Gaps may remain.
A good Threat Hunting report therefore records the search scope, data sources, assumptions, observation period, and unknown areas alongside its findings.
C32's central concept: Tier 3 performs more complex security analysis. Threat Hunting proactively seeks hidden attack evidence before a clear alert has been received.

sections.heading: V. C33 | SOC Manager: managing a SOC differs from directing each security incident

body.text: 1. The SOC Manager manages the security monitoring capability
Suppose that a Silicon Valley technology company has 12 SOC analysts working shifts to monitor several cloud products.
The SOC Manager considers personnel, processes, budgets, and delivery quality alongside technical issues.
Typical duties include scheduling, training, triage processes, tool quality, service commitments, case backlogs, and continual improvement.
For example:
If one SIEM rule generates 2,000 alerts with no investigative value every day, analysts may become overwhelmed by noise and overlook important incidents.
An individual Tier 1 analyst cannot fully resolve this problem.
The SOC Manager should require detection improvements, allocate resources appropriately, and check whether the processes still meet security objectives.
2. How can SOC operating quality be measured?

rows: What is the average time from the defined event start to detection?
How long after an alert does someone acknowledge ownership?
Mean Time to Respond / Recover, etc.
Measure response, repair or recovery using explicitly defined endpoints.

FP/(FP+TN): the proportion of actually negative observations incorrectly classified as positive. FP means false positive and TN true negative. The false-alert proportion is instead FP/(TP+FP), where TP means true positive; the denominators are not interchangeable.
Do escalated cases contain sufficient evidence and the correct priority?

body.text: To assess how much of the alert queue is noise, a SOC can separately measure the false-alert proportion FP/(TP+FP), rather than label it FPR. Both measures require a defined observation period, reference classification and denominator. Sampling only alerted cases generally does not establish all true negatives and therefore cannot, by itself, estimate the full FPR.
These are common operational metrics. Not every SOC must use identical names and formulas.
In particular, MTTR may mean Mean Time to Respond, Repair, Resolve, or Recover in different organizations. Define the starting and ending points explicitly before using it formally.
3. Why not focus only on closing cases quickly?
Suppose that a manager sets this target:
“All alerts must be closed within five minutes.”
To meet the KPI, analysts might label incidents as false positives without sufficient evidence.
The reports then look excellent while detection quality deteriorates.
This is a typical Proxy Metric Problem.
The actual objective is to improve the accuracy and timeliness of detection, analysis, and response at a reasonable cost, rather than simply minimizing ticket lifetime.
The SOC Manager should therefore assess handling time alongside sampled case reviews, missed-detection checks, detection coverage, and response outcomes.
C33's central concept: the SOC Manager is responsible for ongoing SOC operations and management quality, and is not necessarily the commander of every major incident.

sections.heading: VI. C34 | Incident Response Commander: who has authority to decide what happens next?

body.text: 1. A major security incident requires decisions across departments
Suppose that an equipment maintenance management system at a semiconductor fab may have been compromised.
The security team proposes immediately isolating the affected servers.
Manufacturing, however, points out:
“Disconnecting now could remove necessary equipment management functions, affecting production and physical safety.”
Legal also notes that some logs must be preserved for subsequent investigation.
If each department acts independently, the consequences may be worse.
The Incident Response Commander's central responsibility is to coordinate the response within authority assigned in advance.
2. The commander need not be the strongest technical specialist
The Incident Commander does not have to personally analyze every packet, memory image, or malware sample.
The commander integrates specialist judgments and manages priorities, authority, and conflicts.

body.name: incidentcoordination
body.caption: Incident Commander and six parallel collaborating teams
body.description: This is an example organization for a major incident. The commander coordinates six teams within predefined authority; the teams are not six sequential handoffs. The organization’s established response plan determines actual authority and roles.

items.title: Incident Commander
items.body: Incident objectives, decisions, escalation, coordination and communication

items.title: Security / SOC
items.body: Investigate attacks and preserve evidence

items.title: IT / Cloud
items.body: Containment, remediation and infrastructure recovery

items.title: OT / Operations
items.body: Equipment safety and process continuity

items.title: Legal / Compliance
items.body: Compliance, notification and evidence requirements

items.title: Business Continuity
items.body: Alternative processes and business continuity

items.title: Communications
items.body: Internal and external messaging and stakeholders

body.text: This is an example organizational design for a major incident. The enterprise's pre-established response plan determines actual authority and role allocation.
3. Key incident response decisions
The Incident Commander may need to coordinate judgments on:

rows: Should a major security incident be declared?
Technical evidence, business impact, and incident criteria
Ongoing attack risk, isolation consequences, and alternatives
Service impairment and ability to sustain critical business activities
Should customers or authorities be notified?
Incident facts, contracts, and applicable notification obligations
Trustworthy system state, remediation verification, and business approval

body.text: Pre-established authority and decision rules enable the responsible people to make timely, traceable decisions; the commander does not make every decision alone.

NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3 treats incident response as an ongoing risk-management capability. NIST CSF 2.0 RS.MA-01–05 covers response plan execution, incident validation, prioritization, escalation, and criteria for initiating recovery.
4. The distinction between SOC Manager and Incident Commander

rows: Situational assessment, response decisions, and coordination

body.text: In a smaller enterprise, one person may hold both roles, but their responsibilities and authority should still be defined separately.
C34's central concept: the Incident Commander turns cross-departmental information into coherent, timely, traceable response actions.

sections.heading: VII. C35 | Business Continuity Plan (BCP): how can an enterprise operate during disaster?

body.text: 1. BCP sustains business beyond restarting servers
Suppose that a bank's online banking system suffers a ransomware attack.
The IT team may need hours to restore the servers.
But the bank cannot answer only:
“We are fixing the computers.”
It must also consider:

items: Which important financial activities must continue?
Are alternative transaction or service channels available?
Which activities can be temporarily deferred?
How will customers learn the service status?
Are other banking systems affected?
When can an acceptable service capability be restored?

body.text: This is the purpose of a BCP.
A Business Continuity Plan describes how an organization sustains necessary business functions during and after a major disruption.
NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1 defines BCP as predetermined procedures that ensure important business processes continue during and after significant disruption.
A BCP can cover earthquakes, power outages, supply-chain interruptions, equipment failures, and other major events as well as cyber incidents.
2. BCP, DRP, and Incident Response Plan
These three documents are easily confused.

rows: How should a cyber incident be investigated, contained, and handled?
How can affected systems and infrastructure recover after a major disaster?
How can critical business continue while normal systems are unavailable?

body.text: Suppose that a semiconductor company's Manufacturing Execution System (MES) develops a major problem.
The IRP addresses whether malicious compromise occurred and how to isolate, investigate, and contain the incident.
The DRP addresses restoring the MES's technical functions using standby resources and trustworthy backups.
The BCP additionally addresses which manufacturing activities must stop while the MES is unavailable, which may use approved alternative procedures, and how to ensure personnel and equipment safety.
These plans support one another, but none replaces the others.
3. Business Impact Analysis (BIA): why establish priorities first?
BIA is a foundation of BCP.
BIA goes beyond listing systems to ask:
What happens if a business activity stops for 10 minutes, one hour, or one day?
For example:

rows: Process scheduling or production control is affected
Customer transactions cannot be processed normally

body.text: ISO 22301:2019 sets international requirements for a Business Continuity Management System (BCMS). ISO/TS 22317:2021 specifically provides BIA implementation guidance.
4. RTO and RPO: distinguish the two targets
RTO, Recovery Time Objective.
The target time within which a system or service should return to the required state.
RPO, Recovery Point Objective.
The pre-incident point in time to which data must be restored. Expressed as an elapsed interval, it can be understood as the period of data loss that can be tolerated.

body.name: recoverytimeline
body.caption: Banking transaction example: RPO 15 minutes and RTO 2 hours
body.description: These values are teaching targets, not measured results or fixed regulatory requirements. RPO concerns the time window of data loss; RTO concerns time to restore service. Each requires separate backup, recovery and exercise validation. Segments show the actual 15:120 (1:8) time ratio, with labels arranged separately to avoid overlap on narrow screens. This teaching example starts the RTO clock at incident point 0. Actual start and end criteria must be defined by business needs and recovery plans; this does not imply that every NIST scenario starts the clock at the incident.

items.title: Recovery point | 15 minutes before the incident (−15 min)
items.body: RPO (Recovery Point Objective) = 15 minutes: the target point for data recovery.

items.title: Incident | 0 min
items.body: Timeline reference point: start of the system disruption.

items.title: Recovery target | 2 hours after the incident (+120 min)
items.body: RTO (Recovery Time Objective) = 2 hours: the target to restore required service capability. The interval from the incident to this target is the system disruption and recovery period.

body.text: NIST SP 800-34 Rev. 1's terminology explicitly distinguishes Recovery Time Objective and Recovery Point Objective.
A further logical point matters:
Backing up every 15 minutes does not necessarily achieve a 15-minute RPO, nor establish that recovery will finish within two hours.
Consider whether backups succeed, are consistent, remain uncompromised, and can actually be restored at the necessary speed.
5. Taiwanese financial supervision requirements for business continuity

Article 12 of the FSC's Regulations Governing the Implementation of Internal Control and Audit Systems of Financial Holding Companies and Banking Industries explicitly includes business continuity management mechanisms among the policies and operating procedures that internal control must cover.
The same article also covers major contingency handling and confidentiality of customer information.
Financial institutions must apply these requirements to actual business processes and systems.

The Bankers Association's Financial Institutions' Information and Communication Security Protection Baseline and Security Control Operational Standards for Financial Institutions Conducting Electronic Banking Business are self-regulatory references for reviewing related security practice.
6. The role of ISO 22301
ISO 22301 specifies BCMS requirements. The BCP is an important plan and deliverable within that management system.
As of November 2026, ISO 22301:2019 remains the principal published edition, with Amendment 1:2024; a subsequent revision is still under development.
C35's central concept: BCP sustains important business activities, beyond bringing IT systems back online.

sections.heading: VIII. C36 | Service Level Agreement (SLA): how do service commitments become verifiable responsibilities?

body.text: 1. An SLA specifies service quality and responsibilities
Suppose that a Silicon Valley cloud company supplies an AI API to a Taiwanese bank.
The provider says:
“Our system is highly stable, and we have professional customer support.”
This statement provides no specific measurement criteria.
The bank cannot clearly determine what counts as service failure, how quickly the provider must respond, or what happens when commitments are missed.
An SLA supplies those definitions.

NIST's definition of Service Level Agreement encompasses provider responsibilities, customer expectations, reliability, service levels, response times, and arrangements for reporting, resolution, and termination.
2. What can a complete SLA specify?

rows: Time to first response after a severe incident is reported
Targets and responsibilities for repair or restoration
Monitoring data used to calculate service levels
Frequency and method of service reports
Remedies when service commitments are missed

body.text: These are possible SLA design elements; the parties must agree the actual conditions.
3. What does 99.9% availability mean?
Suppose that an SLA commits to monthly availability of 99.9% under its definition.
For a full 30-day month of 24-hour days, with no additional exclusions:
That permits approximately 43.2 minutes during the month that do not meet the availability conditions.
An actual SLA must first define what “unavailable” means and how it is calculated.
For example, if the login page works but every principal transaction API fails, is the service available?
An inappropriate health-check endpoint could show normal service while customers cannot actually use it.
An SLA therefore defines a verifiable service, not merely a percentage.
4. The distinction among SLA, RTO, and RPO

rows: What service quality will the provider deliver?
How soon must the required capability recover?
How much data loss is tolerable?
Must they have identical binding force?
Depends on business objectives and contractual or regulatory requirements
Depends on business objectives and contractual or regulatory requirements

body.text: A provider can commit to both availability and an RTO, but neither can be inferred from the other.
An SLA may also exclude some failure scenarios, so examine the actual agreement.
C36's central concept: an SLA agrees service levels and responsibilities; it does not replace a business continuity plan or confidentiality agreement.

sections.heading: IX. C37 | Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA): what does it protect?

body.text: 1. An NDA permits defined use while establishing confidentiality
Suppose that a Taiwanese semiconductor company commissions a US security consultant to assess a manufacturing-data exchange platform.
The consultant may need access to:

items: System architecture diagrams.
Database structures.
Unpublished technical information.
Vulnerability information obtained during testing.
Confidential customer or supplier information.

body.text: Information provided for a particular job does not grant unrestricted rights to copy, use, or publish it.
The parties therefore need explicit confidentiality obligations.
A Non-Disclosure Agreement contractually constrains the use, retention, and disclosure of particular information.
A Mutual NDA imposes confidentiality obligations on both parties; a Unilateral NDA imposes them on one party.
2. Which questions should a complete NDA answer?

rows: For which purposes may it be used?
Which confidentiality measures must the recipient implement?
Which information falls outside the restrictions?
How long do confidentiality obligations last?
How will information be returned or sanitized when cooperation ends?
What happens when applicable law requires disclosure?

body.text: An NDA should not obstruct lawful reporting to authorities or other legally protected disclosures.
3. Taiwanese semiconductors: NDA and the Trade Secrets Act
Article 2 of Taiwan's Trade Secrets Act requires protected information to be secret, economically valuable because of its secrecy, and subject to reasonable measures by its owner to maintain secrecy.
Article 10 addresses certain improper acquisition, use, or disclosure of trade secrets, including improper methods such as breach of confidentiality obligations.
An NDA can therefore be an important part of reasonable confidentiality measures.
However, the reverse inference is invalid:
“Marking a document Confidential or signing an NDA automatically makes every piece of information a legally protected trade secret.”
The statutory elements and actual protective measures still require examination.
4. US Silicon Valley: the Defend Trade Secrets Act
US federal law, 18 U.S.C. §1839(3), also requires owners to take reasonable secrecy measures and requires the information to derive independent economic value from not being generally known.

18 U.S.C. §1833(b) provides immunity from civil and criminal liability under US federal and state trade-secret law for qualifying confidential disclosures to a US federal, state or local government official, or to an attorney, solely to report or investigate a suspected legal violation. This is not blanket immunity for every disclosure; §1833(b)(5) also does not authorize otherwise unlawful access to obtain trade secrets.
NDA obligations must therefore be understood together with applicable law.
5. Connecting NDA with C15 vulnerability disclosure
Suppose that a security consultant discovers a serious vulnerability in a semiconductor platform.
The consultant should provide appropriately protected testing evidence through the authorized, agreed reporting channels.
An NDA does not automatically replace:

items: Testing authorization.
Scope and Rules of Engagement (ROE).
Vulnerability reporting processes.
Security incident notification procedures.
Data deletion and sanitization requirements.

body.text: These documents address different questions and must be coordinated.
C37's central concept: an NDA governs confidentiality, use, and disclosure of particular information, rather than service availability or permission to operate systems.

sections.heading: X. C38 | Acceptable Use Policy (AUP): why do enterprises need one?

body.text: 1. Access to a system does not permit unrestricted use
Suppose that a bank engineer has a company-issued laptop.
The engineer uses it daily, but may the engineer:

items: Upload customer data to a personal cloud drive?
Analyze internal banking documents with a private AI service?
Install unapproved remote-control software?
Lend company equipment to another person?
Copy production data to a personal test computer?

body.text: Firewalls alone cannot resolve all these questions.
The enterprise must define reasonable uses and prohibited behavior for information assets.
This is the AUP's purpose.
2. How does AUP differ from access control?
Access Control concerns whether a particular operation is technically possible.
An Acceptable Use Policy concerns whether the organization permits that behavior.
For example, an employee may technically be able to install software while organizational policy prohibits unapproved tools in production environments.
Therefore:
Technical ability to perform an action does not imply organizational permission.
This illustrates a distinction between governance and technical controls.
3. The formal NIST SP 800-53 mapping

NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 PL-4, Rules of Behavior, requires organizations to give people needing system access rules on their responsibilities and behavior concerning information and system use, obtain necessary acknowledgement and agreement, and periodically review the rules.
Its supplemental guidance also identifies Acceptable Use Agreements and Non-Disclosure Agreements as related types of access agreement.
An AUP therefore needs review after its initial acknowledgement at onboarding.
4. Designing AUPs for three industries

rows: Maintenance computers, USB devices, manufacturing process data
Restrict unapproved software, external media, and data transfers
SaaS development environments, cloud credentials, source code
Define rules for personal cloud services, external AI tools, and production credentials
Customer data, transaction systems, employee devices
Restrict customer-data queries, personal-device use, and unapproved services

body.text: These are risk-based organizational policy options. They do not imply identical legal requirements for every enterprise.

For Taiwanese banks, Article 12 of the FSC's Regulations Governing the Implementation of Internal Control and Audit Systems of Financial Holding Companies and Banking Industries requires internal controls to cover information management and customer-data confidentiality. Article 25 addresses security arrangements, risk control, and incident notification and response. An AUP can serve as an organizational control implementing those arrangements.
5. How can an AUP become a verifiable control?
An effective AUP works with technical controls.
For example:

rows: Prohibit confidential-data uploads to personal clouds

body.text: These controls may not prevent every violation, but they help prevent, detect, and verify policy enforcement.
C38's central concept: an AUP defines permitted use of information assets. It sets governance rules rather than service levels or confidentiality agreements.

sections.heading: XII. Integrated governance in three industries

body.text: 1. Taiwan's semiconductor technology industry
Suppose that an equipment supplier's remote-maintenance account is misused.
SOC: detect anomalous logins and subsequent operations, and establish incident evidence.
Incident Response: coordinate equipment engineering, IT, OT, and business management to avoid inappropriate isolation actions that could compromise process safety.
BCP: ensure that the fab can sustain necessary manufacturing activities or shut down safely under approved alternative procedures.
SLA: agree response and service-restoration responsibilities with equipment or cloud suppliers.
NDA / AUP: govern suppliers' confidentiality obligations for process data and permitted uses of remote tools and accounts.
References include NIST SP 800-82 Rev. 3, SEMI E187, and Articles 2 and 10 of Taiwan's Trade Secrets Act.
NIST and SEMI provide technical and industry standards; the Trade Secrets Act has legal force.
2. US Silicon Valley technology industry
Suppose that an administrator account at a SaaS company is compromised and an attacker may access customer data.
The SOC detects and analyzes; the Incident Commander coordinates engineering, legal, customer service, and management; BCP sustains important product functions.
For governance, SLA binds service commitments, NDA governs confidential information received by suppliers, and AUP governs system use by internal administrators and developers.
Technical references include NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 3, NIST SP 800-53, the OWASP Logging Cheat Sheet, and MITRE ATT&CK T1078.
The US Defend Trade Secrets Act provides a legal basis for trade-secret definitions and protection. The actual effect of an SLA, NDA, or AUP still depends on applicable law and its specific terms.
3. Taiwanese financial institutions under FSC supervision
Suppose that a major cyberattack affects a bank's core financial services.
The FSC's Regulations Governing the Implementation of Internal Control and Audit Systems of Financial Holding Companies and Banking Industries are directly relevant:

headers: Governance work connected with this chapter

Customer-data confidentiality, major contingency handling, business continuity management

Security risk control, incident notification, response, and CIA protection

body.text: These provisions come from the official FSC legal system. Under Article 55, the May 6, 2026 amendment took effect on publication, with commencement of Articles 44–47 separately determined by the competent authority; the table's Articles 9, 12, 24 and 25 are outside that deferred group. Separately, Article 54 requires financial holding companies and banking enterprises that do not meet its listed institutional requirements to adjust by December 31, 2027. The covered provisions include Article 9, Article 12 paragraph 1 subparagraph 2 item 13 (business continuity management), and Articles 24 and 25, among others, for the institutional matters specified in Article 54. It also gives credit cooperatives the same adjustment deadline for the specified sustainability-information disclosure in internal audit reports. sections.heading: XV. Understanding check: an integrated C30–C38 case

body.text: This case asks you to act as a cross-border security incident response coordinator, beyond recognizing terminology.
Scenario: an attack affects a semiconductor manufacturer and the financial-services supply chain
A Taiwanese semiconductor equipment manufacturer uses a Silicon Valley SaaS platform to manage equipment maintenance records and uses financial services from a Taiwanese bank.
At 02:00, the following events occur:
Event A: the SOC detects a supplier maintenance account logging in from an unusual location, followed by unexpected data access.
Event B: Tier 1 cannot determine whether the account is compromised. Advanced analysts discover that it logged in from an unapproved device.
Event C: the security team recommends immediately isolating the equipment management server, but manufacturing worries about a production interruption.
Event D: the US SaaS platform then becomes unavailable, preventing the Taiwanese semiconductor company from retrieving necessary maintenance information.
Event E: the supplier states that its SLA guarantees only 99.9% monthly availability and does not commit to any specific recovery time.
Event F: investigation discovers that an employee copied confidential equipment records to an unapproved personal cloud account.
Answer:
1. SOC and incident determination: what should Tier 1 and Tier 3 each do for A and B? What evidence is needed to decide whether to declare a security incident?

2. Incident command and authority: who should coordinate the decision in C? What are the respective responsibilities of the SOC Manager, Incident Commander, manufacturing manager, and compliance personnel?
3. Business continuity: for D, how would you establish BIA, RTO, RPO, and alternative business procedures? Which controls require verification through actual exercises?
4. Contract governance: why are monthly availability and RTO not interchangeable in E? As the customer, which service commitments would you request?
5. Confidentiality and acceptable use: which different NDA and AUP obligations are principally involved in F? Which elements of Taiwan's Trade Secrets Act might also be relevant?

6. Supervision and supply chains: if the system also affects important business at a Taiwanese bank, how should the bank use the FSC internal-control requirements and Bankers Association security and supply-chain requirements to establish incident notification, supplier oversight, and business continuity procedures?

These six questions test whether you can integrate SOC responsibilities, incident command, business continuity, service commitments, confidentiality, and use policies into security governance capability.

The unit's central conclusion: mature incident handling starts with reliable detection, proceeds through clear responsibilities and decisions, sustains necessary business, and uses evidence, organizational arrangements, and contracts to drive improvement.
